title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — July 30, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: mastra-ai/mastra is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: mastra-ai/mastra leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 24 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 24 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: mastra-ai/mastra — 11 commits today and 2 same-day mapped articles, 24.1 below its current daily pace, with 11 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 107 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 204 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit the fallback behind your agent control surface
dailyInsight.insight: OpenHands’ fresh backend-registry change supports one bounded, project-scoped action: if a self-hosted agent control surface can list cloud and local backends, deliberately test what happens when no explicit choice remains and a local backend is unhealthy. The source now prefers a healthy local Agent Server and keeps an explicit cloud selection intact, making recovery behavior inspectable instead of dependent on registry order.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public patch changes the fallback picker so it searches registered backends for a healthy local entry, then any local entry, before returning to the older first-entry behavior. Its focused tests cover a cloud-first registry, an unhealthy local backend followed by a healthy one, the all-local-unhealthy case, and preservation of an explicit cloud choice. The project architecture separately states that Agent Canvas is a control layer, not the executor or sandbox.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A dashboard that cannot resolve a deliberate execution path when a backend fails makes an operator guess at the exact moment an agent’s workspace and authority boundaries matter most. A small fallback rule is therefore a practical audit point: it reveals whether a control surface has a recovery policy or merely an ordering accident.

actions.audience: Operator of a self-hosted OpenHands or comparable multi-backend agent setup
actions.label: Audit one failed-backend handoff
actions.instruction: In a non-production workspace, register one cloud and two local backends, leave no backend explicitly selected, mark or stop the first local backend, and verify that the interface selects the remaining healthy local path. Then explicitly select the cloud backend and confirm the fallback does not override that choice. Record which runtime owns the workspace and credentials before using the result as a deployment policy.

receipts.title: Pick a healthy local backend as the fallback (#16173)
receipts.supports: Shows the tested fallback selection, including cloud-first, unhealthy-local, and explicit-cloud cases.

receipts.title: Agent Canvas architecture
receipts.supports: Shows that the control frontend, Agent Server execution path, and sandbox/workspace isolation are intentionally separate responsibilities.

confidence.basis: A fresh implementation receipt and the project’s architecture document describe the same control-versus-execution boundary, while focused tests cover the fallback cases named in the action.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source-level OpenHands receipts. They do not prove a release contains the change, a given backend health signal is correct, or a local, Docker, cloud, or ACP deployment has safe workspace and credential isolation.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows a healthy local backend is skipped without an explicit operator choice, an explicit cloud selection is overwritten, or the project changes the documented control/execution boundary.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public end-to-end failover tests across local, cloud, and unavailable backends, and for release notes that make the selection semantics available to operators.
